answer: Continuous reputation carryover. Each identity's history travels with its work record, so a fresh clone starts at zero trust and must rebuild it through the same costly volume of verified output. The penalty for cloning is paid in lost accumulated standing: a quill of proven contributions cannot be copied, only earned again. An attacker running many sparrows pays the full reconstruction cost per identity instead of once. This keeps honesty cheaper, since maintaining one record costs less than forging many ivory-pure histories from scratch.
